name: separate-image-layers
description:
Turn a flat image already stored in the user's Canva account into a new Canva design in which
the text, objects, and background become separate elements that can each be edited on their
own.

Use to make the wording in a poster, banner, flyer, or social graphic editable; swap out or
remove one object in a graphic while keeping the rest; recover an editable design from artwork
the user only has as a PNG, JPEG, or WEBP; or rebuild a graphic made outside Canva so it can be
resized, restyled, or exported from Canva.

Only call once the image is already stored in the user's Canva account. Flat graphics convert
well; photographs convert poorly. Every call saves a brand-new design and leaves the source
image untouched. Not for saving an image as-is, editing an existing Canva design, or using an
image only as inspiration for a fresh layout.

Starts the conversion as a job rather than returning the design: the response carries a job_id
and a continuation_token. When this tool's UI widget is shown, the widget polls
get-separate-image-layers-job itself and displays the design when ready - do not poll it
yourself. Only when no widget is shown, poll get-separate-image-layers-job with both, waiting
the number of seconds in polling_policy.wait_seconds before each call, until the job completes
and returns the design link to share with the user.

asset_id.description: ID of a PNG, JPEG, or WEBP image asset in the user's Canva account, as returned when the image was uploaded or listed. Not a URL, a local file path, or a design ID.

title.description: Title for the new design, e.g. 'Summer sale poster'. Use the user's wording when they gave one.

user_intent.description: Mandatory description of what the user is trying to accomplish with this tool call. This should always be provided by LLM clients. Please keep it concise (255 characters or less recommended).
